module_name_en: Core Words III and Graded Reading
block_note: The last six texts, and the longest. Level 55 turns from narrative to the opinion paragraph, which is a different shape again: a claim, a concession, a counter, and a refusal to settle it. The module's final word is विदाई, built with the -ई suffix taught in level 2 — the first pattern in the module returning in its last item.

grammar_prep_card.title_en: Active and State Participles (करते हुए, किया हुआ)
grammar_prep_card.explanation_en: Hindi uses participles as adjectives to describe ongoing or completed states. The imperfect participle with 'हुए' (e.g., 'हँसते हुए') describes simultaneous background actions: 'वो हँसते हुए अंदर आए' (He came in laughing). The perfective participle with 'हुआ' (e.g., 'रखा हुआ', 'खड़ा हुआ') describes settled states: 'दरवाज़े पर खड़ा हुआ आदमी' (The man standing at the door) or 'लिखी हुई किताब' (The written book). These agree in gender and number with the noun they modify.

examples.hindi: मेज़ पर रखी हुई किताब मेरी है।
examples.read_as: mez par rakhii huii kitaab merii hai.
examples.english: The book kept on the table is mine.

lines.hindi: फ़ोन मेज़ पर पड़ा था।
lines.read_as: fon mez par paṛaa thaa.
lines.english: The phone lay on the table.

lines.hindi: मैंने उसे तीन बार उठाया और तीन बार रख दिया।
lines.read_as: maiṁne use tiin baar uṭhaayaa aur tiin baar rakh diyaa.
lines.english: I picked it up three times and put it down three times.

lines.hindi: कुछ भी नहीं आया था।
lines.read_as: kuchh bhii nahiiṁ aayaa thaa.
lines.english: Nothing had come.

lines.hindi: रिपोर्ट कल आनी थी। कल बीत गया।
lines.read_as: riporṭ kal aanii thii. kal biit gayaa.
lines.english: The report was due yesterday. Yesterday went past.

lines.hindi: सुबह से मैंने चाय चार बार बनाई और एक बार भी पूरी नहीं पी।
lines.read_as: subah se maiṁne chaay chaar baar banaaii aur ek baar bhii puurii nahiiṁ pii.
lines.english: Since morning I had made tea four times and not once finished it.

lines.hindi: काम में मन नहीं लगा।
lines.read_as: kaam meṁ man nahiiṁ lagaa.
lines.english: I could not settle to work.

lines.hindi: अजीब बात है — बुरी ख़बर से भी ज़्यादा तकलीफ़ इंतज़ार में होती है।
lines.read_as: ajiib baat hai — burii ḳhabar se bhii zyaadaa takliif iṁtazaar meṁ hotii hai.
lines.english: It is a strange thing — waiting hurts more than bad news does.

lines.hindi: बुरी ख़बर के बाद आदमी कुछ करता है।
lines.read_as: burii ḳhabar ke baad aadmii kuchh kartaa hai.
lines.english: After bad news a person does something.

lines.hindi: इंतज़ार में कुछ नहीं कर सकते।
lines.read_as: iṁtazaar meṁ kuchh nahiiṁ kar sakte.
lines.english: In waiting there is nothing you can do.

lines.hindi: बस बैठे रहते हैं और घड़ी देखते हैं।
lines.read_as: bas baiṭhe rahte haiṁ aur ghaṛii dekhte haiṁ.
lines.english: You just sit and watch the clock.

lines.hindi: शाम को फ़ोन बजा। नंबर कोई और था।
lines.read_as: shaam ko fon bajaa. nambar koii aur thaa.
lines.english: In the evening the phone rang. It was a different number.

lines.hindi: मैंने काट दिया और फिर वहीं बैठ गया।
lines.read_as: maiṁne kaaṭ diyaa aur phir vahiiṁ baiṭh gayaa.
lines.english: I cut the call and sat back down where I was.

lines.hindi: बेचैनी की सबसे बुरी बात यही है — उसका कोई काम ही नहीं होता।
lines.read_as: bechainii kii sabse burii baat yahii hai — uskaa koii kaam hii nahiiṁ hotaa.
lines.english: The worst thing about restlessness is that it has no work to do.

learn.title_en: बे- is the seventh way of saying not
learn.explanation_en: बेचैनी is बे- plus चैन, the ease you met in level 47 alongside सुकून and शांति. बे- came in through Persian and is enormously productive: बेचैन restless, बेकार useless, बेवकूफ़ foolish, बेशक without doubt, बेहतर better. That makes seven negating devices in this module — निः- and its forms, ला-, अ- and अन-, बिना, ना-, ग़ैर-, and now बे-. Four of the seven came from Persian and Arabic and three from Sanskrit, and each attaches to words from its own side.
learn.register_note_en: बेचैनी (everyday and literary alike) · व्याकुलता (Sanskrit-side, formal and rare) · घबराहट (closer to panic, and built with the -आहट suffix).
vocabulary_notes: मन नहीं लगा — for the mind not to settle. The mind is the subject.
बीत गया — of time, to pass. बीतना is intransitive, so no ने.
काट देना — to cut a call, the same phrase as in the level 48 doorway narrative.

game.question_en: Why does the piece mention making tea four times and finishing none of it?
options: It is a physical sign of the state the piece only names at the end
He was too busy to drink it
He was saving it for later
game.explanation_en: The word बेचैनी does not appear until the last line. Everything before it is evidence — the phone picked up and put down, the tea, the clock.

lines.hindi: पहला हफ़्ता सबसे लंबा था।
lines.read_as: pahlaa haftaa sabse laṁbaa thaa.
lines.english: The first week was the longest.

lines.hindi: कमरा किराए का था और सामान अभी डिब्बों में।
lines.read_as: kamraa kiraae kaa thaa aur saamaan abhii ḍibboṁ meṁ.
lines.english: The room was rented and my things were still in boxes.

lines.hindi: शाम को बाहर निकलता तो सब लोग किसी न किसी के साथ दिखते।
lines.read_as: shaam ko baahar nikaltaa to sab log kisii na kisii ke saath dikhte.
lines.english: When I went out in the evening, everyone seemed to be with somebody.

lines.hindi: मैं अकेला चलता और वापस आ जाता।
lines.read_as: maiṁ akelaa chaltaa aur vaapas aa jaataa.
lines.english: I would walk alone and come back.

lines.hindi: भाषा वही थी, पर लहजा अलग था।
lines.read_as: bhaaṣaa vahii thii, par lahjaa alag thaa.
lines.english: The language was the same, but the accent was different.

lines.hindi: दुकानदार मेरी बात समझ लेते, फिर भी कुछ अलग रहता।
lines.read_as: dukaandaar merii baat samajh lete, phir bhii kuchh alag rahtaa.
lines.english: Shopkeepers understood me, and still something stayed different.

lines.hindi: रात में ऊपर वाले फ़्लैट से बर्तनों की आवाज़ आती रहती थी।
lines.read_as: raat meṁ uupar vaale flaiṭ se bartanoṁ kii aavaaz aatii rahtii thii.
lines.english: At night the sound of dishes kept coming from the flat above.

lines.hindi: अकेलापन और तन्हाई एक चीज़ नहीं है।
lines.read_as: akelaapan aur tanhaaii ek chiiz nahiiṁ hai.
lines.english: Being alone and loneliness are not the same thing.

lines.hindi: अकेलापन जगह की बात है — कमरे में कोई नहीं होता।
lines.read_as: akelaapan jagah kii baat hai — kamre meṁ koii nahiiṁ hotaa.
lines.english: Being alone is about a place — there is nobody in the room.

lines.hindi: तन्हाई भीड़ में भी हो सकती है।
lines.read_as: tanhaaii bhiiṛ meṁ bhii ho saktii hai.
lines.english: Loneliness can happen in a crowd.

lines.hindi: उस हफ़्ते मैं भरी सड़क पर तन्हा था।
lines.read_as: us hafte maiṁ bharii saṛak par tanhaa thaa.
lines.english: That week I was lonely on a full street.

lines.hindi: फिर एक दिन नीचे वाली दुकान के भैया ने पूछा — नए आए हो?
lines.read_as: phir ek din niiche vaalii dukaan ke bhaiyaa ne puuchhaa — nae aae ho?
lines.english: Then one day the man in the shop below asked — new here?

lines.hindi: बस इतना ही।
lines.read_as: bas itnaa hii.
lines.english: That was all.

lines.hindi: पर उस रात नींद जल्दी आ गई।
lines.read_as: par us raat niiṁd jaldii aa gaii.
lines.english: But that night sleep came early.

learn.explanation_en: अकेलापन in line 8 is अकेला plus -पन, and that suffix builds masculine abstract nouns: बचपन childhood, लड़कपन boyhood, पागलपन madness, and अपनापन in the next item. It is only the second masculine noun-maker this module has shown, after -आव in चुनाव and बदलाव — against five feminine ones. And notice what this text does in lines 8 to 10: it defines its own key word, distinguishing अकेलापन, a fact about a place, from तन्हाई, a fact about a feeling.
learn.register_note_en: तन्हाई (Urdu-side, and the word of songs and poetry) · अकेलापन (everyday and neutral) · एकांत (Sanskrit-side, and usually solitude that is chosen rather than suffered).
vocabulary_notes: किसी न किसी के साथ — with somebody or other. The doubled किसी makes it vague on purpose.
लहजा — accent or tone of speech, masculine.
नींद आना — for sleep to come. The sleep does the arriving, as in the level 47 narrative.

practice.question_en: What did the shopkeeper say to him?
options: He asked where he was from
He asked whether he was new here

game.question_en: What changed for him that day?
options: Nothing material — being noticed by one person was enough
He decided to leave the city
game.explanation_en: बस इतना ही insists that the event was tiny. The next line, about sleep, is the only evidence that it mattered.

items.target_gloss_en: the feeling of being treated as one's own

lines.hindi: गाड़ी रास्ते में ख़राब हो गई।
lines.read_as: gaaṛii raaste meṁ ḳharaab ho gaii.
lines.english: The car broke down on the way.

lines.hindi: शाम हो रही थी और आसपास दूर तक कोई कस्बा नहीं था।
lines.read_as: shaam ho rahii thii aur aaspaas duur tak koii kasbaa nahiiṁ thaa.
lines.english: It was getting dark and there was no town for a long way around.

lines.hindi: थोड़ी दूर पर एक घर दिखा।
lines.read_as: thoṛii duur par ek ghar dikhaa.
lines.english: A house came into view a little way off.

lines.hindi: मैंने दरवाज़ा खटखटाया।
lines.read_as: maiṁne darvaazaa khaṭkhaṭaayaa.
lines.english: I knocked at the door.

lines.hindi: एक बुज़ुर्ग निकले। मैंने बात बताई।
lines.read_as: ek buzurg nikle. maiṁne baat bataaii.
lines.english: An old man came out. I explained.

lines.hindi: उन्होंने कुछ नहीं पूछा — न नाम, न काम, न कहाँ से आया हूँ।
lines.read_as: unhoṁne kuchh nahiiṁ puuchhaa — na naam, na kaam, na kahaaṁ se aayaa huuṁ.
lines.english: He asked nothing — not my name, not my work, not where I had come from.

lines.hindi: बस अंदर बुला लिया।
lines.read_as: bas aṁdar bulaa liyaa.
lines.english: He simply called me inside.

lines.hindi: चाय आई, फिर खाना आया।
lines.read_as: chaay aaii, phir khaanaa aayaa.
lines.english: Tea came, then food came.

lines.hindi: उनकी पत्नी ने पूछा कि रोटी और चाहिए क्या।
lines.read_as: unkii patnii ne puuchhaa ki roṭii aur chaahie kyaa.
lines.english: His wife asked whether I wanted more roti.

lines.hindi: मैंने पैसे देने की कोशिश की। उन्होंने हाथ पकड़ लिया और मना कर दिया।
lines.read_as: maiṁne paise dene kii koshish kii. unhoṁne haath pakaṛ liyaa aur manaa kar diyaa.
lines.english: I tried to give them money. He took my hand and refused.

lines.hindi: रात उन्हीं के यहाँ कटी।
lines.read_as: raat unhiiṁ ke yahaaṁ kaṭii.
lines.english: The night passed there.

lines.hindi: सुबह मैकेनिक आया और गाड़ी ठीक हो गई।
lines.read_as: subah maikenik aayaa aur gaaṛii ṭhiik ho gaii.
lines.english: In the morning a mechanic came and the car was mended.

lines.hindi: उन्होंने रास्ता भी समझा दिया।
lines.read_as: unhoṁne raastaa bhii samjhaa diyaa.
lines.english: He explained the road to me as well.

lines.hindi: जाने से पहले मैंने शुक्रिया कहा। उन्होंने सिर्फ़ इतना कहा — फिर आना।
lines.read_as: jaane se pahle maiṁne shukriyaa kahaa. unhoṁne sirf itnaa kahaa — phir aanaa.
lines.english: Before leaving I thanked him. All he said was — come again.

lines.hindi: अपनापन कोई बड़ी चीज़ नहीं होती।
lines.read_as: apnaapan koii baṛii chiiz nahiiṁ hotii.
lines.english: अपनापन is not a large thing.

lines.hindi: वो बस यही है — किसी अजनबी के लिए दरवाज़ा खोल देना।
lines.read_as: vo bas yahii hai — kisii ajnabii ke lie darvaazaa khol denaa.
lines.english: It is only this — opening the door for a stranger.

learn.explanation_en: अपना is one's own; अपनापन, with the -पन suffix from the last item, is the quality of being treated as one's own. English has warmth, and belonging, and neither is it. The nearest thing English can do is a phrase, and the piece knows this, which is why it ends by defining the word with an action rather than a synonym. Note also हाथ पकड़ लिया in line 10: पकड़ना from level 50 and not थामना, because this is a firm stopping gesture rather than a tender one.
learn.register_note_en: अपनापन (warm, everyday) · आत्मीयता (Sanskrit-side, the same idea in formal writing) · मेहमाननवाज़ी (Persian-derived, and specifically the practice of hospitality rather than the feeling behind it).
vocabulary_notes: बुज़ुर्ग — an elderly person, from level 16, and here taking the respectful plural निकले.
उन्हीं के यहाँ — उन plus ही plus यहाँ: at their very house.
फिर आना — the infinitive as a soft imperative, and the whole weight of the ending is in it.

practice.question_en: What did the old man ask him?
practice.explanation_en: Line 6: न नाम, न काम, न कहाँ से आया हूँ.

game.question_en: What do the questions he did not ask and the money he would not take have in common?
options: He wanted the visitor to leave quickly
He was suspicious of the visitor
Both refuse to make it a transaction — nothing is asked and nothing is owed
game.explanation_en: Asking who somebody is, and being paid, are both ways of settling an account. The piece removes them one after the other.

summary.recap_en: बे- is the seventh negating device in this module, and four of the seven came in from Persian and Arabic. -पन builds masculine abstract nouns — अकेलापन, बचपन, अपनापन — and is only the second masculine noun-maker against five feminine ones. And two of these three pieces define their own key word rather than translating it.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the last two texts of the module, and a different shape — the opinion paragraph.

lines.hindi: हर बड़े फ़ैसले से पहले एक दौर आता है।
lines.read_as: har baṛe faisle se pahle ek daur aataa hai.
lines.english: Before every big decision there is a period.

lines.hindi: दोनों रास्ते ठीक लगते हैं और दोनों में कुछ खोना पड़ता है।
lines.read_as: donoṁ raaste ṭhiik lagte haiṁ aur donoṁ meṁ kuchh khonaa paṛtaa hai.
lines.english: Both roads look right, and either way something has to be given up.

lines.hindi: इसी हालत को कशमकश कहते हैं।
lines.read_as: isii haalat ko kashmakash kahte haiṁ.
lines.english: This state is what कशमकश means.

lines.hindi: लोग कहते हैं कि दिल की सुनो।
lines.read_as: log kahte haiṁ ki dil kii suno.
lines.english: People say listen to your heart.

lines.hindi: पर दिल भी दो बातें कहता है।
lines.read_as: par dil bhii do baateṁ kahtaa hai.
lines.english: But the heart says two things as well.

lines.hindi: और अक्सर दोनों बातें सच होती हैं।
lines.read_as: aur aksar donoṁ baateṁ sach hotii haiṁ.
lines.english: And often both of them are true.

lines.hindi: कुछ लोग कहते हैं कि काग़ज़ पर दोनों तरफ़ के फ़ायदे लिख लो।
lines.read_as: kuchh log kahte haiṁ ki kaaġaz par donoṁ taraf ke faayde likh lo.
lines.english: Some people say write the advantages of both sides on paper.

lines.hindi: मैंने कई बार लिखे। कभी काम नहीं आया।
lines.read_as: maiṁne kaii baar likhe. kabhii kaam nahiiṁ aayaa.
lines.english: I have written them many times. It has never helped.

lines.hindi: आप फ़ायदे गिन सकते हैं, डर नहीं।
lines.read_as: aap faayde gin sakte haiṁ, ḍar nahiiṁ.
lines.english: You can count advantages. You cannot count fear.

lines.hindi: सूची लंबी हो जाती है और फ़ैसला वहीं का वहीं रहता है।
lines.read_as: suuchii laṁbii ho jaatii hai aur faislaa vahiiṁ kaa vahiiṁ rahtaa hai.
lines.english: The list gets longer and the decision stays exactly where it was.

lines.hindi: शायद असली बात यह है कि कशमकश का कोई हल नहीं होता।
lines.read_as: shaayad aslii baat yah hai ki kashmakash kaa koii hal nahiiṁ hotaa.
lines.english: Perhaps the real point is that a dilemma has no solution.

lines.hindi: वो सिर्फ़ ख़त्म होती है — किसी एक दिन, अचानक।
lines.read_as: vo sirf ḳhatm hotii hai — kisii ek din, achaanak.
lines.english: It only ends — one day, suddenly.

lines.hindi: और उस दिन भी यक़ीन नहीं होता कि चुनाव सही था।
lines.read_as: aur us din bhii yaqiin nahiiṁ hotaa ki chunaav sahii thaa.
lines.english: And even that day you are not sure the choice was right.

lines.hindi: बस इतना होता है कि इंतज़ार करना मुमकिन नहीं रहता।
lines.read_as: bas itnaa hotaa hai ki iṁtazaar karnaa mumkin nahiiṁ rahtaa.
lines.english: It is only that going on waiting stops being possible.

learn.title_en: The shape of an opinion paragraph
learn.explanation_en: This is not a story, and it moves differently. Watch the pattern: a claim in lines 1 to 3, then लोग कहते हैं कि — other people's view — followed immediately by पर. Then a second view, कुछ लोग कहते हैं कि, and again a counter. Then शायद असली बात यह है कि, which is how a Hindi opinion piece announces its own position. Concede, counter, concede, counter, then state. That structure is worth recognising because almost every column in a Hindi newspaper uses it.
learn.register_note_en: कशमकश (Urdu-side, an inner tug-of-war) · दुविधा (Sanskrit-side — दु, two, plus विधा, way) · असमंजस (also Sanskrit-side, and closer to bewilderment than to being torn).
vocabulary_notes: दौर — a period or phase, masculine.
वहीं का वहीं — exactly where it was, unmoved. The doubling is what carries the meaning.
मुमकिन नहीं रहता — stops being possible. From मुमकिन in level 28.

practice.question_en: What does the writer say about making a list?
options: It works if you are patient
He has tried it and it has never helped
practice.explanation_en: Line 8: मैंने कई बार लिखे। कभी काम नहीं आया.

game.question_en: According to the piece, how does a dilemma actually end?
options: A list eventually makes it clear
It is never solved — waiting simply stops being possible
game.explanation_en: Line 11 removes the idea of a solution and line 14 supplies what happens instead. Neither line says it alone.

lines.hindi: आजकल सब एक ही सवाल पूछते हैं — और कैसा चल रहा है?
lines.read_as: aajkal sab ek hii savaal puuchhte haiṁ — aur kaisaa chal rahaa hai?
lines.english: These days everyone asks the same question — so how are things going?

lines.hindi: जवाब भी सबका एक ही होता है — बस, बहुत व्यस्त हूँ।
lines.read_as: javaab bhii sabkaa ek hii hotaa hai — bas, bahut vyast huuṁ.
lines.english: And everyone's answer is the same — oh, very busy.

lines.hindi: व्यस्त होना अब एक तारीफ़ बन गया है।
lines.read_as: vyast honaa ab ek taariif ban gayaa hai.
lines.english: Being busy has become a compliment.

lines.hindi: किसी से पूछिए कि छुट्टी में क्या किया — जवाब मिलेगा, कुछ ख़ास नहीं।
lines.read_as: kisii se puuchhie ki chhuṭṭii meṁ kyaa kiyaa — javaab milegaa, kuchh ḳhaas nahiiṁ.
lines.english: Ask somebody what they did on their holiday — the answer will be, nothing much.

lines.hindi: खाली वक़्त वाले आदमी से लोग पूछते हैं कि आजकल क्या कर रहे हो।
lines.read_as: khaalii vaqt vaale aadmii se log puuchhte haiṁ ki aajkal kyaa kar rahe ho.
lines.english: People ask the man with free time what he is doing these days.

lines.hindi: सवाल में ही शक होता है।
lines.read_as: savaal meṁ hii shak hotaa hai.
lines.english: The suspicion is in the question itself.

lines.hindi: पर फ़ुर्सत आलस नहीं है।
lines.read_as: par fursat aalas nahiiṁ hai.
lines.english: But leisure is not laziness.

lines.hindi: आलस में काम नहीं होता। फ़ुर्सत में काम होता है, बस जल्दी नहीं होती।
lines.read_as: aalas meṁ kaam nahiiṁ hotaa. fursat meṁ kaam hotaa hai, bas jaldii nahiiṁ hotii.
lines.english: In laziness nothing gets done. In leisure things get done, only without hurry.

lines.hindi: फ़र्क़ रफ़्तार का है, नीयत का नहीं।
lines.read_as: farq raftaar kaa hai, niiyat kaa nahiiṁ.
lines.english: The difference is one of speed, not of intent.

lines.hindi: पुराने लोग शाम को छत पर बैठते थे और कुछ नहीं करते थे।
lines.read_as: puraane log shaam ko chhat par baiṭhte the aur kuchh nahiiṁ karte the.
lines.english: People of an older generation would sit on the roof in the evening and do nothing.

lines.hindi: हम उसे बर्बादी कहते हैं।
lines.read_as: ham use barbaadii kahte haiṁ.
lines.english: We call that a waste.

lines.hindi: शायद वो उसे ज़िंदगी कहते थे।
lines.read_as: shaayad vo use ziṁdagii kahte the.
lines.english: Perhaps they called it living.

lines.hindi: मुझे नहीं पता कि कौन सही है।
lines.read_as: mujhe nahiiṁ pataa ki kaun sahii hai.
lines.english: I do not know which of us is right.

lines.hindi: पर इतना पता है कि जल्दी में कोई चीज़ पूरी तरह याद नहीं रहती।
lines.read_as: par itnaa pataa hai ki jaldii meṁ koii chiiz puurii tarah yaad nahiiṁ rahtii.
lines.english: But I do know that nothing done in a hurry is remembered properly.

learn.title_en: फ़ुर्सत, and defining a word by saying what it is not
learn.explanation_en: फ़ुर्सत is the state of not being pressed for time, and English has no single word for it — leisure is close but suggests idleness in a way फ़ुर्सत does not. So the piece defines it by exclusion: फ़ुर्सत आलस नहीं है, and then the difference is रफ़्तार rather than नीयत. That move is very common in Hindi opinion writing, and it is worth noticing as a technique rather than only reading for content.
learn.register_note_en: फ़ुर्सत (Urdu-side, and warm) · अवकाश (Sanskrit-side, and the same word as a formal holiday, from the level 8 sign) · खाली वक़्त (plain, and slightly negative — empty time).
vocabulary_notes: रफ़्तार — speed, feminine, Urdu-side. नीयत — intention, also feminine.
बर्बादी — waste or ruin, feminine, with the -ई suffix from level 2.
शक — doubt or suspicion, masculine, and here located in the question rather than in a person.

practice.question_en: What does the writer say the difference between leisure and laziness is?
options: One is respectable and one is not
One is chosen and one is not
practice.explanation_en: Line 9: फ़र्क़ रफ़्तार का है, नीयत का नहीं.

game.question_en: What is शायद doing in line 12?
options: Offering their view without claiming it, which the next line then confirms
Saying the two words mean the same thing
Asserting that the older generation was right
game.explanation_en: The piece could have ended by taking a side. शायद hands the reader the other view, and मुझे नहीं पता refuses to settle it.

lines.hindi: दफ़्तर में उनका आख़िरी दिन था।
lines.read_as: daftar meṁ unkaa aaḳhirii din thaa.
lines.english: It was his last day in the office.

lines.hindi: सुबह से सब कुछ सामान्य चल रहा था।
lines.read_as: subah se sab kuchh saamaanya chal rahaa thaa.
lines.english: Everything had been ordinary since the morning.

lines.hindi: वो हमेशा की तरह साढ़े नौ बजे आए और अपनी जगह बैठ गए।
lines.read_as: vo hameshaa kii tarah saaṛhe nau baje aae aur apnii jagah baiṭh gae.
lines.english: He came at half past nine as always and sat down in his place.

lines.hindi: दोपहर में एक छोटा सा कार्यक्रम रखा।
lines.read_as: dopahar meṁ ek chhoṭaa saa kaaryakram rakhaa.
lines.english: A small gathering was held at midday.

lines.hindi: किसी ने कुछ लंबा नहीं कहा।
lines.read_as: kisii ne kuchh laṁbaa nahiiṁ kahaa.
lines.english: Nobody made a long speech.

lines.hindi: एक लड़के ने फूल दिए और सबने ताली बजाई।
lines.read_as: ek laṛke ne phuul die aur sabne taalii bajaaii.
lines.english: A young man gave him flowers and everyone clapped.

lines.hindi: चाय और समोसे आए, फिर सब अपनी-अपनी जगह लौट गए।
lines.read_as: chaay aur samose aae, phir sab apnii-apnii jagah lauṭ gae.
lines.english: Tea and samosas came, and then everyone went back to their places.

lines.hindi: उन्होंने सिर्फ़ इतना कहा — बहुत अच्छा लगा, आप सब का शुक्रिया।
lines.read_as: unhoṁne sirf itnaa kahaa — bahut acchhaa lagaa, aap sab kaa shukriyaa.
lines.english: All he said was — it has been good, thank you all.

lines.hindi: शाम को जाने से पहले उन्होंने अपनी मेज़ ख़ाली की।
lines.read_as: shaam ko jaane se pahle unhoṁne apnii mez ḳhaalii kii.
lines.english: Before leaving in the evening he cleared his desk.

lines.hindi: दराज़ में एक पुराना कप था। उसे भी रख लिया।
lines.read_as: daraaz meṁ ek puraanaa kap thaa. use bhii rakh liyaa.
lines.english: There was an old cup in the drawer. He took that too.

lines.hindi: बाईस साल की सारी चीज़ें एक थैले में आ गईं।
lines.read_as: baaiis saal kii saarii chiizeṁ ek thaile meṁ aa gaiiṁ.
lines.english: Twenty-two years of things fitted into one bag.

lines.hindi: निकलने से पहले वो एक बार पीछे मुड़े।
lines.read_as: nikalne se pahle vo ek baar piichhe muṛe.
lines.english: Before going out he turned back once.

lines.hindi: किसी ने नहीं देखा।
lines.read_as: kisii ne nahiiṁ dekhaa.
lines.english: Nobody saw.

lines.hindi: विदाई का सबसे अजीब हिस्सा यही होता है।
lines.read_as: vidaaii kaa sabse ajiib hissaa yahii hotaa hai.
lines.english: This is the strangest part of a farewell.

lines.hindi: बड़ी बातें सब कह देते हैं।
lines.read_as: baṛii baateṁ sab kah dete haiṁ.
lines.english: Everyone says the big things.

lines.hindi: पर आख़िरी नज़र किसी के लिए नहीं होती — वो सिर्फ़ अपने लिए होती है।
lines.read_as: par aaḳhirii nazar kisii ke lie nahiiṁ hotii — vo sirf apne lie hotii hai.
lines.english: But the last look is not for anybody — it is only for yourself.

learn.title_en: विदाई — the first suffix of the module, in its last word
learn.explanation_en: विदाई is विदा, leave-taking, plus the -ई suffix taught in level 2 — feminine, as every noun that suffix builds has been. That is the module's first pattern returning in its hundred and sixty-fifth and final word. विदाई also names the occasion itself: a विदाई समारोह at an office, and the विदाई at a wedding when the bride leaves her family's house. Both are formal, both have a fixed shape, and this piece is about the moment that falls outside it.
learn.register_note_en: विदाई (the occasion of parting) · विदा (the act — विदा लेना, to take one's leave) · अलविदा (the word you actually say). Three related words, three different jobs.
vocabulary_notes: अपनी-अपनी जगह — each to their own place. The doubling distributes it across everybody.
मुड़ना — to turn. मुड़े, respectful plural.
आख़िरी नज़र — the last look. नज़र is feminine, as level 13 established.

practice.question_en: What did he take from the drawer?

game.question_en: Nobody saw him turn back. What does the piece make of that?
options: The look was never for anybody else, so being unseen takes nothing from it
He wanted to be noticed and was not
game.explanation_en: किसी ने नहीं देखा reads as a loss until the last line, which turns it into the point. The whole piece waits for that.

summary.recap_en: An opinion paragraph concedes, counters, concedes again and then states its own position with शायद असली बात यह है कि. A word with no English equivalent gets defined by what it is not. And विदाई closes the module on the -ई suffix that opened it in level 2.
summary.next_up_en: That is all 165 items. Module 14 takes up connected speech — relative clauses, conditionals and the participles this module has been writing around.

module_complete.note_en: Module 13 is complete. The 105 vocabulary items and the 60 reading target words are 165 distinct words, which is what holds the app at 480 words in total.
open_flags: Reading texts avoid the passive with जाना, relative-correlative clauses and participial constructions, because Module 14 teaches all three. This is most strained in the news block at levels 38 to 47, where a real report would use the passive constantly. Worth deciding whether reading items may contain a not-yet-taught form for recognition only.

Five reading targets were repointed during generation because the planned word had already appeared in an earlier text or gloss. Four of those five were forward references written from a vocabulary card to a later reading item. A vocabulary card should not name an upcoming reading target.
